risks: Low. Risks for dogs are hunger, too-rapid weight loss and reduced pain relief; nurses follow a maximum weekly loss of 2 percent and any welfare concern is referred to the vet. Owners' risk is inconvenience.
consent: Written informed consent from the owner after an information sheet explaining allocation, visits and that usual care continues in either group; owners may withdraw at any time without affecting their dog's care.
data: Owner names and addresses stay in practice systems; the trial database holds study numbers, practice and dog data; videos are stored without owner identifiers.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus applied to owners: income (diet discount for both groups), distance from the practice (phone check-ins), age and disability (exercise plans adapted to what owners can do), and language (information sheet in the two most common local languages). Enrolment by practice is monitored so that practices in poorer areas are not under-represented.
effectiveness: The trial answers whether the clinic improves mobility enough to justify roll-out; a null result would save nurse time for other care.
efficiency: Uses existing nurses, the existing index and one review visit for usual care.
costs: Nurse time covered by the group; the diet discount funded by the manufacturer with no role in the study; video scoring by vets within existing time.
grants: None needed; a positive result could support a veterinary nursing research award for a cost analysis of roll-out.
partnerships: Practice nurse champions, the group board, two owner representatives from the group's client panel, and the diet manufacturer only as a supplier.
rebPath: Approved by the practice group's clinical research ethics committee for client-owned animals on 2026-09-02 (CREC-2026-022); welfare stopping rules are part of the approval.
limitations: Owners cannot be blinded; six months may be too short for long-term weight maintenance; one practice group.
summary: Low-risk trial in client-owned dogs with written owner consent, welfare stopping rules and owner-level equity measures.
